title: It All Belongs to God
key_points: Everything belongs to God; He owns it all and has placed a portion in our hands as stewards.
God requires stewards to be faithful, not brilliant or wealthy.
In the parable of the talents, unequal amounts are judged only by faithfulness with what was received.
The servant who buried his talent out of fear shows that doing nothing with God's goods is loss, not neutral.

verse.text: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts.

scene.caption: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine.
scene.alt: Coins and a scale rest beside an open Bible under a golden, ray-lit sky, showing that all things belong to God.

title: Tithes, Offerings, and Firstfruits
key_points: Tithing began with Abraham long before the law, given freely to Melchizedek out of worship.
Malachi calls the withheld tithe robbery and invites Israel to test God's promised blessing.
The Lord Jesus Christ upheld tithing while rebuking neglect of judgment, mercy, and faith.
Giving is to be purposed beforehand in the heart and offered cheerfully, not under pressure.

verse.text: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

scene.caption: God loveth a cheerful giver.
scene.alt: A sheaf of grain and a pile of coins are brought before a temple in the early dawn light.

title: Sowing and Reaping
key_points: Sowing and reaping is a fixed law of balance woven into all creation, and God is not mocked.
Sparing sowing yields a sparing harvest, and bountiful sowing yields a bountiful one.
The widow of Zarephath sowed her last meal first, and her supply of meal and oil never failed.
The harvest is not immediate, so believers must sow deliberately and not faint before due season.

verse.text: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.

scene.caption: Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.
scene.alt: A sheaf of grain stands beside a path leading toward a sunlit horizon, a picture of sowing and reaping.

title: Debt, Work, and Contentment
key_points: The borrower is servant to the lender, so debt costs a measure of freedom.
Christians are to owe no man anything except the ongoing debt of love.
Scripture commands honest work and providing for one's own house, and rebukes idleness.
Godliness with contentment is great gain, while the love of money brings many sorrows.

verse.text: But godliness with contentment is great gain.

scene.caption: Godliness with contentment is great gain.
scene.alt: A broken chain lies near a tree and a few coins, showing freedom from debt through honest work and contentment.

title: Money in the House of God
key_points: Ananias and Sapphira sinned not by the amount withheld but by giving a false gift for appearance.
Paul refused to carry the collection alone so it would be honest before God and visibly honest before men.
Elders who labour in the Word are worthy of support but must be free from the love of money.
The offering exists to feed the work of God and to remember the widow, the poor, and the persecuted.

verse.text: Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.

scene.caption: Providing for honest things in the sight of men.
scene.alt: A scale, coins, and a lamp rest on a table, showing money in the house of God handled openly and honestly.
